subsystems.name: Ingredient streams
subsystems.role: supply food-grade proteins, fats, carbohydrates and micronutrients pure enough to be dosed precisely.

subsystems.name: Ink formulation
subsystems.role: turns those streams into printable pastes and gels with controlled flow behaviour.

subsystems.name: Print head
subsystems.role: deposits several materials at once at sub-millimetre resolution.

subsystems.name: Dosing and control
subsystems.role: keeps each portion's nutrient profile on target and the structure geometrically accurate.

subsystems.name: Structure setting
subsystems.role: fixes the printed shape so it survives cooking, shipping and eating.

subsystems.name: Quality and safety
subsystems.role: proves the product is nutritious, stable and safe.

buildSteps.title: Make pure ingredient streams
buildSteps.detail: Proteins are grown in fermentation tanks by engineered microbes and separated from the broth; lipids are fractionated; vitamins and minerals are bought as purified food-grade powders.

buildSteps.title: Characterise each batch
buildSteps.detail: Purity, molecular-weight distribution, water content and allergen profile are measured, because printing tolerances are tighter than in ordinary cooking.

buildSteps.title: Formulate printable inks
buildSteps.detail: Protein, fat, water and binder are blended until the paste has enough yield stress to hold its shape but still flows through a nozzle, while vitamins are protected from heat and oxygen.

buildSteps.title: Load the print head
buildSteps.detail: Separate cartridges hold protein matrix, fat, micronutrient concentrate and flavour, so their ratios can be varied voxel by voxel.

buildSteps.title: Print layer by layer
buildSteps.detail: The head traces a toolpath laying down roughly 0.1–1 mm strands, embedding fat droplets and nutrient pockets inside a protein scaffold. This is printing at millimetre scale — true one-molecule-at-a-time assembly is not a known process.

buildSteps.title: Set the structure
buildSteps.detail: Mild heat, ionic or enzymatic crosslinking locks the printed geometry so it does not collapse.

buildSteps.title: Cook and finish
buildSteps.detail: The piece is baked, seared or dried to develop texture and browning, then packed under modified atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Verify and release
buildSteps.detail: Samples are assayed for vitamin retention and protein content, screened for microbes, and tasted before release.

prerequisites.why: it can already make specific proteins cheaply, but volumes and costs are far from food-commodity level.
extrusion printers exist for pastes and cultured tissue, but throughput is far below a food factory's.
food science already protects sensitive micronutrients through processing and storage.

prerequisites.tech: In-line nutrient sensing and closed-loop control
prerequisites.why: keeping every portion within a declared nutrient specification needs fast, cheap measurement that is not yet routine.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory path for novel ingredients and printed foods
prerequisites.why: no framework yet covers a food assembled dose-by-dose from purified compounds.

pathway.milestone: extruded 3D-printed snacks, plant-based analogues and texture-modified foods for people who cannot swallow
pathway.unlocks: proof that printing can shape food reliably.

pathway.milestone: printed products built from fermentation-derived proteins with declared, tunable nutrient profiles
pathway.unlocks: foods engineered for specific diets, from sports nutrition to clinical feeding.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop printers that adjust composition in real time from sensor readings
pathway.unlocks: personalised portions made on demand rather than in bulk.

pathway.milestone: molecular-scale assembly of food from purified building blocks
pathway.unlocks: arbitrary texture and nutrition with almost no agricultural input — still speculative, and limited by thermodynamics, cost and appetite.
